questions.question: Who among the following is known for his/her books ‘The Algebra of Infinite Justice’, ‘Kashmir: The Case for Freedom’ and ‘Capitalism: A Ghost Story’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arundhati Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arundhati Roy:**

 
 
• Arundhati Roy is an Indian author best known for her novel "The God of Small Things," which won the 1997 Man Booker Prize.
 
• She is also a prominent political activist involved in human rights and environmental causes.
 
• "The Algebra of Infinite Justice" is a collection of essays that critically examine the United States' response to the 9/11 attacks.
 
• "Kashmir: The Case for Freedom" is a political essay where she has written about the kashmir issue.
 
• "Capitalism: A Ghost Story" critiques the effects of globalization and capitalism in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jhumpa Lahiri:**

 
 
• Jhumpa Lahiri is an American author of Indian origin known for her short stories and novels.
 
• She won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 2000 for her short story collection "Interpreter of Maladies."
 
• Her works often explore themes of identity, displacement, and cultural adaptation, particularly among Indian immigrants in the United States.
 
• She has also written the novel “The Namesake” and “Unaccustomed Earth”.
 
• In recent years she has been writing in the italian language.
 
 
 
• **Salman Rushdie:**
 
 
• Salman Rushdie is a British-American novelist and essayist of Indian origin.
 
• He is known for his controversial novel "The Satanic Verses," which led to a fatwa calling for his assassination.
 
• His works often blend magical realism with historical and political commentary.
 
• His other famous books include “Midnight’s Children” and “Grimus”.
 
• He is known for his unique writing style.
 
 
 
• **Amitav Ghosh:**
 
 
• Amitav Ghosh is an Indian author known for his historical fiction and non-fiction works.
 
• His works often explore themes of colonialism, climate change, and the history of the Indian Ocean region.
 
• He is the author of "The Shadow Lines," "The Glass Palace," and "The Ibis Trilogy."
 
• He has written non fiction works that discuss the climate crisis.
 
• He is known for his very detailed and well researched books.

questions.question: Few renowned artists of ________ dance style in India are Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak:**

 
 
• Kathak is a major classical dance form originating from northern India.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, rapid spins (chakkars), and expressive gestures.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "katha," meaning "story," and story-telling is a key element of the dance.
 
• Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao, and Kumudini Lakhia are indeed renowned exponents of Kathak, contributing significantly to its evolution and popularization.
 
• Kathak has strong Hindu and Muslim influences, and has evolved through both temple and court traditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau:**

 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical dance form with martial, tribal, and folk traditions.
 
• It originates from the eastern Indian states of Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
 
• Chhau dances are characterized by vigorous movements, acrobatic leaps, and the use of masks in some styles.
 
• The dance often depicts episodes from epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana, as well as local legends.
 
• There are three main styles of Chhau, named after the location where they are performed: Purulia Chhau, Seraikella Chhau, and Mayurbhanj Chhau.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri:**
 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form originating from the northeastern Indian state of Manipur.
 
• It is known for its graceful and fluid movements, particularly the raslila, which depicts the love story of Radha and Krishna.
 
• Manipuri dance uses distinctive cylindrical skirts (called 'kumil') and veils.
 
• The dance emphasizes gentle swaying movements and subtle hand gestures.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the Vaishnavism tradition.
 
 
 
• **Odissi:**
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form originating from the eastern Indian state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its tribhangi (three-bend) posture, graceful movements, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• Odissi dance is deeply rooted in the temple traditions of Odisha, and many of its movements are inspired by sculptures found in ancient temples.
 
• The dance involves expressions of divine and human love.
 
• Odissi was reconstructed in the mid 20th century, after a period of decline.

questions.question: Moti Masjid in Agra fort was constructed by which of the following Mughal Emperors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shahjahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shahjahan:**

 
 
• Shahjahan reigned during the peak of Mughal architectural splendor.
 
• He commissioned the Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) within the Agra Fort, known for its pristine white marble construction.
 
• His most iconic creation is the Taj Mahal, a testament to his love for his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• He also significantly redesigned the Agra Fort, adding numerous marble structures.
 
• Shahjahan built the Jama Masjid in Delhi, another architectural masterpiece.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aurangzeb:**

 
 
• Aurangzeb's reign saw a decline in Mughal architectural patronage.
 
• While he did construct the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, his focus shifted more towards military campaigns and expanding the empire.
 
• His architectural style was less ornate than that of Shah Jahan.
 
• Aurangzeb's rule is often characterized by its strict adherence to Islamic law.
 
• His rule expanded the Mughal empires territory to its largest size.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir:**
 
 
• Jahangir was known for his love of art and gardens.
 
• He continued the construction of Akbar's tomb in Sikandra.
 
• He significantly contributed to the development of Mughal painting.
 
• Jahangir also designed many beautiful gardens.
 
• His rule was known for relative peace, and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Akbar:**
 
 
• Akbar's architectural style blended Persian and Indian influences.
 
• He built the Agra Fort, although Shahjahan later modified it extensively.
 
• He also constructed the city of Fatehpur Sikri, including the Buland Darwaza and Panch Mahal.
 
• He was known for his religious tolerance.
 
• Akbar's rule consolidated the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: To get relief from constipation, which of the following is prescribed to be eaten in large amount?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fibre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fibre:**

 
 
• Dietary fibre, also known as roughage, is the indigestible portion of plant foods.
 
• It adds bulk to the stool, making it easier to pass through the digestive system.
 
• Fibre absorbs water, which softens the stool and prevents constipation.
 
• Consuming a high-fibre diet is a primary recommendation for relieving and preventing constipation.
 
• Good sources of fibre include fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and legumes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protein:**

 
 
• Protein is essential for building and repairing tissues.
 
• While protein is a vital nutrient, it does not directly contribute to relieving constipation.
 
• Excessive protein intake, especially without sufficient fibre, can worsen constipation.
 
• Protein is found in foods like meat, poultry, fish, eggs, and dairy.
 
• Protein is broken down into amino acids.
 
 
 
• **Meat:**
 
 
• Meat is a source of protein and iron.
 
• However, it is generally low in fibre, which can contribute to constipation.
 
• Processed meats often contain high amounts of sodium and unhealthy fats.
 
• Red meat is also known to take longer to digest.
 
• A diet high in meat and low in fibre can exacerbate constipation.
 
 
 
• **Fish:**
 
 
• Fish is a good source of protein and omega-3 fatty acids.
 
• Like meat, fish is low in fibre and does not directly relieve constipation.
 
• Omega-3 fatty acids have anti-inflammatory properties, but they do not have a significant impact on bowel movements.
 
• Fish is a lean source of protein.
 
• Some fish contain high levels of vitamin D.

questions.question: In 1974, classical singer Naina Devi was awarded the Padma Shri for her contribution to which of the following singing styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thumri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thumri:**

 
 
• Thumri is a semi-classical vocal genre originating from the Uttar Pradesh region of India.
 
• It is characterized by its lyrical and romantic nature, often expressing themes of love and devotion.
 
• Thumri emphasizes emotional expression and improvisation, with a focus on conveying the mood of the lyrics.
 
• Naina Devi was a renowned exponent of Thumri, known for her expressive and evocative renditions.
 
• Thumri often uses Braj Bhasha, a dialect of Hindi, for its lyrics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tappa:**

 
 
• Tappa is a semi-classical vocal genre that originated in the Punjab region of India.
 
• It is characterized by its fast-paced and intricate melodic patterns.
 
• Tappa songs often express themes of love and longing.
 
• It is known for its quick turns and complex ornamentation.
 
• Tappa requires great skill and vocal agility.
 
 
 
• **Kajari:**
 
 
• Kajari is a semi-classical vocal genre associated with the monsoon season in northern India.
 
• It is characterized by its folk-like melodies and lyrics that celebrate the beauty of nature and the joys of the rainy season.
 
• Kajari songs often express themes of love, longing, and separation.
 
• It is traditionally performed during the Hindu month of Shravan.
 
• Kajari is very popular in the regions of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Dadra:**
 
 
• Dadra is a light classical vocal genre that is closely related to Thumri.
 
• It is characterized by its lighter and more playful mood compared to Thumri.
 
• Dadra songs often feature themes of love and romance, but in a more lighthearted manner.
 
• It is known for its rhythmic variations and improvisations.
 
• Dadra is often performed with a faster tempo than Thumri.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for the compound commonly known as 'laughing gas'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**N2**____**O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **N2O (Nitrous Oxide):**

 
 
• Nitrous oxide is commonly known as 'laughing gas' due to its euphoric effects when inhaled.
 
• It is a colorless, non-flammable gas with a slightly sweet odor and taste.
 
• It is used in medical and dental procedures as an anesthetic and analgesic.
 
• It is also used as a propellant in aerosol cans and as an oxidizer in rocket motors.
 
• In high concentrations, it can cause asphyxiation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NO (Nitric Oxide):**

 
 
• Nitric oxide is a free radical that plays a crucial role in various biological processes.
 
• It is a signaling molecule involved in vasodilation, neurotransmission, and immune response.
 
• It is also a pollutant produced by combustion processes.
 
• It is a colorless gas.
 
• It is used in some medical treatments.
 
 
 
• **N2O3 (Dinitrogen Trioxide):**
 
 
• Dinitrogen trioxide is an unstable oxide of nitrogen.
 
• It is a dark blue liquid or solid that decomposes at room temperature.
 
• It is an intermediate in the production of nitric acid.
 
• It is a strong oxidizing agent.
 
• It is very toxic.
 
 
 
• **NO2 (Nitrogen Dioxide):**
 
 
• Nitrogen dioxide is a reddish-brown gas with a pungent, irritating odor.
 
• It is a major air pollutant produced by combustion processes, particularly from vehicles.
 
• It contributes to the formation of smog and acid rain.
 
• It can cause respiratory problems.
 
• It is a strong oxidizing agent.

questions.question: In which of the following religions was the agriculture prohibited for its followers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jainism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jainism:**

 
 
• Jainism strongly emphasizes the principle of Ahimsa (non-violence) towards all living beings.
 
• Agriculture is often prohibited for strict Jain followers because it inevitably involves harming living organisms, such as insects and microorganisms in the soil.
 
• Jains believe that even unintentional harm carries karmic consequences.
 
• This is why many Jains traditionally pursue occupations such as trade and commerce.
 
• Jain monks and nuns especially adhere to strict rules to avoid causing any harm.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhism:**

 
 
• Buddhism emphasizes the Middle Way, avoiding extremes of asceticism and indulgence.
 
• While Buddhism promotes compassion for all living beings, it does not strictly prohibit agriculture.
 
• Buddhist monks and nuns often rely on alms from lay followers, which may include agricultural produce.
 
• Buddhist teachings focus on achieving enlightenment through meditation and ethical conduct.
 
• Buddhism has varying views on different occupations, but agriculture is not universally prohibited.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism:**
 
 
• Vaishnavism is a Hindu tradition that centers on the worship of Vishnu or his avatars, such as Krishna and Rama.
 
• Vaishnavism encourages a devotional path to spiritual liberation.
 
• Agriculture is a common occupation among Vaishnavas, and agricultural produce is often offered as prasad (sacred food).
 
• Vaishnavism emphasizes vegetarianism and non-violence, but agriculture is not prohibited.
 
• Many Vaishnavas believe that offering the product of their labor to god is a part of their devotional practice.
 
 
 
• **Shaivism:**
 
 
• Shaivism is a Hindu tradition that centers on the worship of Shiva.
 
• Like Vaishnavism, Shaivism does not prohibit agriculture.
 
• Shaivites engage in various occupations, including agriculture, and often offer agricultural produce in their rituals.
 
• Shaivism emphasizes asceticism and yogic practices, but it does not impose a general prohibition on agriculture.
 
• Shaivism has a diverse range of practices and philosophies.

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Indian Arms Act, 1878, was passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Lytton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Lytton:**

 
 
• Lord Lytton served as the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880.
 
• He was responsible for enacting the Indian Arms Act of 1878, which restricted Indians from possessing firearms.
 
• This act was highly controversial and seen as discriminatory, fueling anti-British sentiment.
 
• His administration was also marked by the disastrous handling of the Great Famine of 1876-1878.
 
• He was also the viceroy during the second Anglo-Afghan war.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Curzon:**

 
 
• Lord Curzon served as the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905.
 
• He is known for his policies of centralization and efficiency, but also for his divisive actions, such as the partition of Bengal in 1905.
 
• He implemented reforms in education, agriculture, and archaeology.
 
• He was known for his interest in preserving ancient monuments.
 
• His rule was a time of increased nationalism.
 
 
 
• **Lord Ripon:**
 
 
• Lord Ripon served as the Viceroy of India from 1880 to 1884.
 
• He is remembered for his liberal policies, including the repeal of the Vernacular Press Act and the introduction of local self-government.
 
• He attempted to pass the Ilbert Bill, which aimed to remove racial jurisdiction disparities in the courts.
 
• His rule is often viewed as a time of progressive reform.
 
• He is considered one of the most popular viceroys.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dufferin:**
 
 
• Lord Dufferin served as the Viceroy of India from 1884 to 1888.
 
• His tenure saw the annexation of Upper Burma in 1885.
 
• The Indian National Congress was founded during his viceroyalty in 1885.
 
• His rule was a time of increased British expansion.
 
• His rule was a time of increased political organization by Indians.

questions.question: Which Article deals with the provisions in case of failure of the constitutional machinery in the State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 356**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 356:**

 
 
• Article 356 of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions in case of failure of the constitutional machinery in a state.
 
• It empowers the President of India to impose President's Rule in a state if the Governor reports that the state government cannot function according to the Constitution.
 
• This article is often referred to as "President's Rule" or "State Emergency."
 
• The President's Rule results in the suspension of the state government, and the state comes under the direct control of the central government.
 
• This article has been a subject of much debate and controversy regarding its use and misuse.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 448:**

 
 
• Article 448 does not exist within the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Indian Constitution contains 448 articles, but those articles are within parts and schedules, and also some are deleted.
 
• Therefore 448 is not related to any specific legal provision.
 
• The last article in the constitution is 395.
 
• Any number higher than that is not a valid article number.
 
 
 
• **Article 395:**
 
 
• Article 395 deals with the repeal of the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
• It signifies the transition from British rule to the establishment of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This article effectively abolished the legal framework of the colonial era.
 
• It is the final article of the indian constitution.
 
• This Article is important for the legal history of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 342:**
 
 
• Article 342 deals with the specification of Scheduled Tribes.
 
• It empowers the President to specify the tribes or tribal communities that shall be deemed to be Scheduled Tribes in relation to that state or union territory.
 
• It is crucial for the implementation of affirmative action policies for Scheduled Tribes.
 
• This article allows for the protection of tribal communities.
 
• The list of scheduled tribes can be modified by parliament.

__
 
• **Parliamentary System Origin:**

 
 
• The parliamentary system of government originated in Britain.
 
• It is characterized by the fusion of the executive and legislative branches of government.
 
• The head of government, the Prime Minister, is chosen from the legislature (Parliament).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Adoption:**

 
 
• India adopted the parliamentary system from Britain due to its historical association and familiarity with the system.
 
• The British had established a parliamentary framework in India through various acts prior to independence.
 
• The framers of the Indian Constitution found the parliamentary system suitable for India's diverse population and democratic aspirations.
 
• The system allows for greater accountability of the executive to the legislature.

questions.question: According to average rainfall in India, the Ladakh Union Territory is located in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**areas of inadequate rainfall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"Low Rainfall" as a Classification:**

 
 
• Indian meteorological classifications typically use terms like "low rainfall" to categorize regions with specific precipitation ranges.
 
• Ladakh's consistently very low annual precipitation fits squarely within these established classifications for arid or semi-arid regions.
 
• Geographically, the term accurately reflects the region's position in the rain shadow of the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **"Inadequate Rainfall" as a Contextual Term:**
 
 
• "Inadequate rainfall" is more of a contextual term, implying that the rainfall is insufficient for a particular purpose (e.g., agriculture, water supply).
 
• While Ladakh's rainfall is indeed inadequate for many purposes, the primary classification is based on the measured precipitation levels.
 
• Ladakh's terrain is such that even if the rainfall was higher, traditional agriculture would have limited success.
 
• The term inadequate can also be a subjective term.
 
 
 
• **Ladakh's Specific Situation:**
 
 
• Ladakh's unique geography and climate make it an area of consistently low rainfall, not just a place where rainfall is sometimes inadequate.
 
• The region is a cold desert.

questions.question: Due to the popularity of Indian clothes in Britain, a law was passed to ban Indian clothes. Which of the following was that law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calico Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calico Act:**

 
 
• The Calico Acts were a series of English laws passed between 1700 and 1721.
 
• They were designed to protect the British wool and silk industries from the competition of imported cotton textiles, particularly calico, from India.
 
• Calico was a type of cotton fabric, often printed with intricate designs, that had become immensely popular in Britain.
 
• The acts initially banned the import of finished calico and later extended to prohibit the wearing of calico.
 
• These acts demonstrate the economic impact of Indian textiles on the British market during that period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muslin act:**

 
 
• There is no historically recognized "Muslin Act" in the context of British laws against Indian textiles.
 
• Muslin, another fine cotton fabric from India, was also popular, and its trade was affected by the general restrictions on Indian textiles.
 
• Muslin was a very high quality fabric.
 
• Muslin was desired by the wealthy.
 
• The trade in Muslin was very profitable.
 
 
 
• **Calso act:**
 
 
• "Calso Act" is not a recognized historical term related to British laws or Indian textiles.
 
• It is likely a misspelling or an incorrect term.
 
• There are no historical records of this act.
 
• It is important to use accurate historical names.
 
• Historical accuracy is very important.
 
 
 
• **Textile act:**
 
 
• While there were numerous acts related to textiles in British history, "Textile Act" is too general a term.
 
• The specific laws that targeted Indian textiles were the Calico Acts.
 
• The term textile act does not refer to one specific law.
 
• Many laws relating to textiles occurred during the industrial revolution.
 
• The Calico acts predated the industrial revolution.

questions.question: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder in teenagers. Here body weight:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**loses drastically**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anorexia Nervosa:**

 
 
• Anorexia nervosa is a serious eating disorder characterized by an intense fear of gaining weight, a distorted body image, and persistent behavior that interferes with weight gain.
 
• Individuals with anorexia nervosa severely restrict their food intake, often leading to drastic weight loss.
 
• They may also engage in excessive exercise or use purging behaviors (such as vomiting or laxative abuse) to control their weight.
 
• This disorder can have severe physical and psychological consequences.
 
• It is a mental health condition with a high mortality rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **does not change:**

 
 
• In anorexia nervosa, body weight does not remain stable.
 
• The core feature of the disorder is a drive for thinness, leading to weight loss.
 
• If a persons weight does not change, then they do not have anorexia nervosa.
 
• Weight change is a key diagnostic factor.
 
• This answer is the opposite of the reality of the disorder.
 
 
 
• **increases slightly:**
 
 
• Slight weight gain is not characteristic of anorexia nervosa.
 
• The disorder is defined by a fear of weight gain and behaviors aimed at preventing it.
 
• Any weight gain causes severe distress to a person with anorexia nervosa.
 
• This answer is contrary to the defining characteristics of the illness.
 
• Weight gain is what people with this illness fear.
 
 
 
• **increases drastically:**
 
 
• Drastic weight gain is not associated with anorexia nervosa.
 
• The disorder leads to significant weight loss due to severe food restriction.
 
• Drastic weight increase is associated with other eating disorders.
 
• This is the opposite of the effect of anorexia nervosa.

questions.question: 'Navroz' is celebrated as the new year by which of the following communities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parsi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parsi:**

 
 
• Navroz, also known as Nowruz, is the Persian New Year, celebrated by the Parsi community, who are followers of Zoroastrianism.
 
• It marks the first day of spring and the renewal of nature.
 
• Parsis celebrate Navroz with traditional rituals, including prayers, feasts, and the setting of a special table called the Haft-sin.
 
• It is a time for family gatherings and the exchange of gifts.
 
• Navroz has pre-Islamic roots, and is a very old celebration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Christian:**

 
 
• Christians celebrate the New Year on January 1st, according to the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Different Christian denominations may have other significant dates related to religious observances, but January 1st is the widely recognized New Year's Day.
 
• Christian celebrations often include church services, family gatherings, and festive meals.
 
• The date of Easter is also a very important date for Christians.
 
• The celebration of christmas is also a major holiday.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist:**
 
 
• Buddhists observe various New Year celebrations depending on their cultural and regional traditions.
 
• In Theravada Buddhist countries like Thailand, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka, the New Year (Songkran) is typically celebrated in April.
 
• In Tibetan Buddhism, Losar is the New Year, which usually falls in February or March.
 
• Buddhist New Year celebrations often involve temple visits, prayers, and community festivities.
 
• Buddhist celebrations often reflect the local culture.
 
 
 
• **Sikh:**
 
 
• Sikhs celebrate Vaisakhi as their New Year, which usually falls on April 13th or 14th.
 
• Vaisakhi also commemorates the formation of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.
 
• Sikh celebrations include visits to gurdwaras, kirtan (devotional singing), and community gatherings.
 
• Vaisakhi is a very important religious holiday.
 
• The celebration is often a very festive occasion.

questions.question: Which of the followings is NOT one of the government accounts of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**General Provident Fund**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **General Provident Fund:**

 
 
• The General Provident Fund (GPF) is a savings scheme for government employees.
 
• It is a contributory provident fund where employees contribute a portion of their salary, and the government pays interest on the accumulated amount.
 
• While the government manages the GPF, it is not considered one of the core government accounts like the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, or Public Accounts.
 
• It is a fund for government employees retirement.
 
• The money in the GPF belongs to the individual government employees.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Accounts of India:**

 
 
• The Public Accounts of India is where funds that do not belong to the government are kept.
 
• These include funds from small savings, provident funds, and other deposits.
 
• The government acts as a banker for these funds.
 
• The government does not have direct control over these funds.
 
• The funds are refundable to the depositor.
 
 
 
• **Consolidated Fund of India:**
 
 
• The Consolidated Fund of India is the most important government account.
 
• All government revenues, loans, and expenditures are routed through this fund.
 
• No money can be withdrawn from this fund without parliamentary approval.
 
• It is the primary source of funds for the government's operations.
 
• It is created by article 266 of the constitution.
 
 
 
• **Contingency Fund of India:**
 
 
• The Contingency Fund of India is used for unforeseen expenditures.
 
• It is at the disposal of the President of India.
 
• It is used for emergency situations.
 
• It is created by article 267 of the constitution.
 
• Parliamentary approval is sought after the expenditure

questions.question: To mark the 75 years of Indo-Lanka Diplomatic Relations, External Affairs Minister Jaishankar inaugurated the 'Geoffrey Bawa: It is Essential To be There' Exhibition in March 2023. Who was Geoffrey Bawa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lankan Architect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Geoffrey Bawa's Profession:**

 
 
• Geoffrey Bawa was a highly influential Sri Lankan architect.
 
• He is considered one of the most important and influential Asian architects of the 20th century.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Style:**
 
 
• He is known for his unique architectural style, which blends modern architectural concepts with traditional Sri Lankan design elements.
 
• His work emphasized the integration of buildings with their natural surroundings.
 
• He was a pioneer of what is known as "tropical modernism."
 
• His designs focused on creating harmonious relationships between indoor and outdoor spaces.
 
 
 
• **Key Contributions:**
 
 
• Bawa's work significantly impacted the development of architecture in Sri Lanka and the broader region.
 
• He designed numerous iconic buildings, including hotels, residences, and public spaces.
 
• His designs often incorporated courtyards, verandas, and water features.
 
• His work often used local materials.
 
• His work was known for its attention to detail.

questions.question: Amer Fort was built with red sandstone and white marble by which ruler in the 16th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Man Singh I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Man Singh I:**

 
 
• Raja Man Singh I was the ruler of Amer (now Jaipur) in the 16th century.
 
• He is credited with the major construction of Amer Fort, using red sandstone and white marble.
 
• He was a trusted general in the Mughal emperor Akbar's army.
 
• His reign saw significant expansion and development of the Amer kingdom.
 
• The fort's architecture reflects a blend of Rajput and Mughal styles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Jai Singh:**

 
 
• Raja Jai Singh II, also known as Sawai Jai Singh, was the founder of the city of Jaipur.
 
• He is known for building the City Palace and Jantar Mantar in Jaipur.
 
• He was a skilled astronomer and city planner.
 
• He lived in the 18th century, much later than the primary construction period of Amer Fort.
 
• He was known for his diplomatic skills.
 
 
 
• **Raja Udai Singh:**
 
 
• Raja Udai Singh II was the founder of the city of Udaipur.
 
• He is known for building the City Palace in Udaipur.
 
• He lived in the 16th century, but his focus was on establishing Udaipur.
 
• He played a key role in the history of Mewar.
 
• He was the father of Maharana Pratap.
 
 
 
• **Raja Amar Singh:**
 
 
• Raja Amar Singh I was the ruler of Mewar.
 
• He was known for his resistance against the Mughal Empire.
 
• He lived in the 17th century.
 
• He was the son of Maharana Pratap.
 
• His rule was marked by conflict with the Mughal empire.
